chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Buying a first property in Quebec when you've just arrived comes with particular challenges: building local credit, understanding a different system, and navigating vocabulary and rules specific to the province. With good support, it's entirely accessible.

This guide gives newcomers key markers: credit and financing, Québec specifics, and the steps to prepare.

Informational content. Each chapter ends with a lined “My notes” page.

Buying a first property in Quebec as a newcomer comes with particular challenges: building local credit, understanding a different system, learning a specific vocabulary. With good support, it's entirely accessible. This guide gives the key markers.

Informational content: validate your situation with the relevant professionals.

chapters.title: Building your credit and financing file
chapters.objective: Making yourself financeable in the local system.
chapters.html:
Making yourself financeable in the local system.

Lenders look at your Canadian credit, your income and your stability. A local credit history can take time to build.

  • Start building credit early (a card, on-time payments).
  • Gather proof of income and employment.
  • Explore newcomer programs, with particular conditions.

The more solid and documented your file, the simpler and more advantageous the financing will be.

Lenders look at your Canadian credit, your income and your stability. A local history takes time to build: open a card as soon as you arrive and pay it in full every month. Some newcomer programs offer suitable conditions, through a mortgage broker.

Emilie's tip

Open a credit card as soon as you arrive and pay it in full every month. Building a Canadian history takes months: start well before you think about buying.

chapters.title: Understanding the Québec specifics
chapters.objective: Learning the local rules of the game.
chapters.html:
Learning the local rules of the game.

The Quebec system has its particularities, often different from what exists elsewhere:

  • The role of the notary (mandatory) and the broker (governed by the OACIQ).
  • Welcome Tax, municipal and school taxes.
  • Co-ownership divided/undivided, leases and rental rules if a plex.
  • Building particularities (clay soils, French drain, heating, winter).

Understanding them in advance avoids many costly surprises.

The Quebec system has its particularities: a mandatory notary, a broker governed by the OACIQ, the Welcome Tax, divided/undivided co-ownership, leases if a plex, and building stock specific to the climate (clay soils, French drain, winter). Learning the local vocabulary already avoids half the mistakes.

Emilie's tip

Take the time to learn the local vocabulary: “Welcome Tax”, “location certificate”, “conditions of the promise to purchase”. Understanding the words already avoids half the mistakes.

chapters.title: Preparing and getting good support
chapters.html:
Moving forward with confidence.

Like any first-time buyer, lay the foundations:

  • Set a realistic budget.
  • Get a mortgage pre-approval.
  • Define your criteria and your areas.

As a bonus, surround yourself with professionals who understand your journey (broker, mortgage broker, notary). Learning the local market before buying is an investment that pays off.

Like any first-time buyer, lay the foundations: a realistic budget, a pre-approval, criteria and areas. As a bonus, surround yourself with professionals used to supporting newcomers — a good broker will explain not only the houses, but the whole system around them.

Emilie's tip

Choose professionals used to supporting newcomers. A good broker will explain not only the houses, but the whole system around them — that's invaluable.

chapters.title: The down payment and the available help
chapters.html:
Gathering and optimizing your contribution.

The minimum down payment depends on the property's price; below a certain threshold, loan insurance is added to the financing.

  • Save early and automate your contributions.
  • Check your eligibility for assistance programs and incentives (depending on your status and situation).
  • A family gift is accepted with a gift letter.

A mortgage broker can help you assemble it all in the most advantageous way.

The minimum down payment depends on the price; under 20%, loan insurance is added. Save early, check your eligibility for assistance programs, and know that a family gift is accepted with a gift letter. A mortgage broker helps you assemble it all advantageously.

Emilie's tip

Look into the programs for first-time buyers and newcomers: some offer advantageous conditions. A mortgage broker knows the ones you're entitled to.

chapters.title: From the search to taking possession
chapters.objective: Following the journey step by step.
chapters.html:
Following the journey step by step.

Once financed and well supported, the buying journey follows a clear logic:

  1. Visit according to your criteria and areas.
  2. Make a promise to purchase with the right conditions (financing, inspection).
  3. Carry out the inspection and fulfill the conditions.
  4. Sign at the notary and take possession.

At each step, ask your questions: no one expects a newcomer to already know the whole system.

The journey follows a clear logic: visit according to your criteria, make a promise to purchase with the right conditions (financing, inspection), fulfill the conditions after the inspection, then sign at the notary. At each step, ask your questions: no one expects a newcomer to already know everything.

Emilie's tip

Don't be afraid to ask “too many” questions. A good professional would a thousand times rather answer your questions than see you sign without understanding. It's your biggest purchase.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Start or consolidate my Canadian credit.
  2. Gather my proof of income and employment.

Within 30 days

  1. Meet a mortgage broker (newcomer programs).
  2. Learn about the Québec specifics.

Next

  1. Get a pre-approval and start my search with Emilie.

To prepare

  1. Build my Canadian credit and gather my proof of income.
  2. Meet a mortgage broker (newcomer programs) and get a pre-approval.
